sample_unit: authentic patient questions (3,130 expert rubric criteria)

links.outcome: Rubric-based completeness of LLMs on real patient pancreatic cancer questions versus exam-style performance
links.effect: Rubric completeness ranged from 46.5% to 82.3% across 22 LLMs despite expert-level exam performance; newer reasoning models did not consistently improve factuality.
links.quote: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved expert-level performance on standardized examinations, yet multiple-choice accuracy poorly reflects real-world clinical utility and safety.

links.outcome: Hallucination rate (responses with at least one factual error) across LLMs
links.effect: Hallucination rates ranged from 6.0% for Gemini-2.5 Pro and GPT-4o to 53.8% for Llama-3.1-8B; o3 produced inaccuracies more often than other GPT-family models.
links.quote: Factual errors were common, with hallucination rates (the percentages of responses containing at least one factual error) ranging from 6.0% for Gemini-2.5 Pro and GPT-4o to 53.8% for Llama-3.1-8B.

links.outcome: Rubric score with versus without web-search grounding
links.effect: Web search did not improve scores: Gemini-2.5 Pro 66.8% to 63.9%; GPT-5 73.8% to 72.8% when web search was enabled.
links.quote: The average score changed from 66.8% to 63.9% for Gemini-2.5 Pro and from 73.8% to 72.8% for GPT-5 when web search was enabled.

unlisted_practices: Expert-authored question-specific rubrics from authentic patient questions versus synthetic AI-generated rubrics for LLM evaluation

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs answering real patient oncology questions on a clinical benchmark, specifically testing the effect of web-search integration on factual correctness and completeness.
